preamble: Devoicing of the voiced affricate /dz/ with concomitant aspiration, yielding /tsʰ/, occurs where a whole voiced series becomes voiceless aspirated. Two independent cases are well documented: the Western Armenian consonant shift, in which Classical Armenian voiced stops and affricates became voiceless aspirates (Eastern Armenian retains /dz/), and the devoicing of Middle Chinese voiced obstruents, which gave aspirates in Mandarin and Cantonese level-tone syllables and in all tones in Hakka.

Middle Chinese voiced initials became aspirated in level-tone (ping) syllables; in oblique tones they became unaspirated (坐 dzwaX > zuò [t͡suo⁵¹]).
Aspirated in the low level (yang ping) tone; vernacular rising-tone 坐 co5 [t͡sʰɔː¹³] 'sit' is also aspirated.
Hakka aspirates Middle Chinese voiced obstruents in all tones, unlike Mandarin zuò.
